utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, 15 minutes for you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Good morning. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Davidovic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, may I tender 3793? I believe it will be of assistance to the Chamber. That's the transcript of Mr. Davidovic's testimony in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In its entirety?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1450, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have these 15 minutes, Mr. Davidovic, so I'll try to shed light on some things that remained unclear. You mentioned some man called Pejo as one of the Arkan's men. Is he one of the locals in Bosnia and Herzegovina or he came from outside, from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even before he came to Bijeljina, he was a well-known criminal. He was investigated by our operative staff. He used to live in Belgrade. He was a member of Arkan's clan. When the war began -- or, rather, during the preparations in Erdut and on the Drina River, he was with Arkan all the time and later became his deputy. He was later given the rank of colonel in the army, led by Arkan, and later he was even given the rank of general.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there a problem among the local population? Were there people who were associated with Arkan?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were, in Bijeljina, people who were associated with Arkan. They even got killed, fighting with him. They had undergone training and later became members of the Arkan's Guard, paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now call up 65 ter 13403.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you - and there is also a translation - do you agree that pursuant to some sort of report, a man responsible for embezzlement is trying to leave and I'm intervening with General Tolimir to have him arrested so that he couldn't leave?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 15 March 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's when he tried to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1451, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I now have 1D3781.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to look at this. Is it the case that on 23rd September 1992 the ministry informs the prime minister and members of the Presidency that the smuggling of weapons in SAO Herzegovina has been stopped; these weapons were smuggled by Serbs, but our police stopped them and arrested them? It's the police who wrote this, and the names are Serb names?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 23rd September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the smugglers are Serbs, judging by the names?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They tried to sell those weapons, the weapons they had been issued with in Republika Srpska. They transferred them across the Drina. And there was even a trial of some people from Ugljevik in Serbia because they tried to sell those weapons or re-sell those weapons in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1452, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3780, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in this paper I inform the Main Staff on 27 January 1994 that representatives of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna will hand over, at some check-point probably, these persons: Svetomir, Sacira, Alen, Denis, all of them last name Brankovic? Is this a Muslim family?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says: "On the same occasion, the sister and the brother-in-law of Osman Karabegovic, Berka and Muharem Osmic from Mostar, will also be handed over. Please give safe passage and complete security to these persons on their way to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Pay special attention to the Osmic married couple." Who was Osman Karabegovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He fought in the war. I think he was even a war veteran from World War II. He had been decorated. And I believe he was also the president of the War Veterans Association.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just clarify for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a war veterans association from the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although we had changed the system, we were a non-Communist Party, we were not anti-Communist. I left the names of some streets named after national heroes from World War II?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We didn't hear your answer, Mr. Davidovic. Could you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This paper is something I support with all my heart. It is an attempt, an effort, to protect the family of Osman Karabegovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll mark this for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1453, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we look at 1D3784.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that my adviser is addressing the Main Staff, on my authority? He's, in fact, writing to the municipalities of Vogosca and Ilijas that the Main Staff had informed me that without the consent of the army, volunteers are being engaged, contrary to the Law on the Army, and that I am asking to be urgently briefed?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those are members of some political party that the local authorities are trying to engage as volunteers, and you're trying to stop it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1454, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see 1D3787.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a bulletin of daily incidents of the Police Security Station in Bijeljina, dated 23rd October 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 2 and the page after so Mr. Davidovic can see to whom this was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Members of the Government of Republika Srpska, Jovo Miskin, the same Jovo Miskin who supported you on behalf of the government in your efforts?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I introduced this bulletin when I came, and there was a person in charge of publishing it. And I wanted the local authorities informed on a daily basis at first, and later also the government in Pale. This bulletin covered all the incidents that happened in one day in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see number 2. Two strangers came into the yard of some Masic, Nurija, and drove away his tractor; investigation is underway.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That was just reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page. But you accept it. You know what it is. It's all recorded. It cannot be covered up because it's documented?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Wherever we have the full names, we record them, and the Internal Affairs organs then took action. But we were not responsible for monitoring what happened later.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1455, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3788, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 26 December 1992, just for you to see that the bulletin you introduced continued. 26 December, page 2, to see who received this? The corps command, garrison command, chief of the CSB, head of the Public Security Station, chief of the National Security, and chief of Crime Investigation.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page. These are the topics you introduced: Crime, public order, and peace. Some people had their documents checked. Some were brought into custody. Next page. Traffic accidents, reprimands issued. There were no foreigners. Next page. What you introduced, in other words, continued?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1456, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You should come to your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two more questions -- or, rather, two more documents. Could I please have that extra time because we actually did not start exactly at 9.00? It would be useful because it really has to do with what the witness knows just before he came. 65 ter 583.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is the 6th of June, 1992, it's the Command of the East Bosnia Corps, and they're issuing an order to rename territorial defence staffs and TO units, thus part of a single Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D1457.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 7402, another one. 7402.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the 3rd of June, also transformation of the guard into units of the Eastern Bosnian Corps? And the order is issued to transform the guard of Semberija-Majevica, and then, further on, one company to the Bircanska Brigade, another one to the Bijeljina MAP? Is that the Volunteer Guard of SAO Semberija that, on the basis of the Territorial Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, can we have the next page, the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mauzer, yes. The Eastern Bosnia Corps is asking for it to be transformed and to become part of a single army; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. This order did exist, but this order was never carried out. Up until the end of the war, the guard did function. It was totally autonomous, independent, and it never wanted to be under the command of the Army of Republika Srpska. There were a great many difficulties involved, and you know that General Mladic warned about that too. It is true that sometime in 1992, in the beginning of July, an active-duty military person, a major by rank, was assigned to that unit after all. Now, was Panta his name or nickname? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know. I know that when he came there, he had a talk at the corps command, and I happened to be there, when it was indicated to him how this separation from the command and the Main Staff would affect everything. This major actually got killed afterwards, and the guard was never transformed into three, the Bircanska and the rest. The guard functioned until the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that Mladic and I came, after some crises had emerged, and I exerted pressure on the president of the municipality, who was a good man except for his inclination towards these territorial units, but Mauzer took his rank and returned him to the rank of private? Have you heard of that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of it. I heard that he was degraded -- rather, that his rank was taken away from him. But he didn't have a rank in the first place. I know that these were problems. I know that there was a lot of brazen behaviour there. At one point in time, there was a lack of respect for your order to have him re-subordinated to the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1458, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Last question, Mr. Davidovic. It was only yesterday that I heard from you that these 15 young men who you had brought were that well trained. At the time, did we have a leader, like yourself, and well-trained young men like them?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The unit that used to be the Special Unit within BH, I mean the Republican MUP, before the war, it fell apart along ethnic lines, and I think that about 10 persons who were ethnic Serbs separated from the unit and moved to the school at Vraca. If you remember, when I first came to Sarajevo, it had to do with an attempt to get that Special Unit that was later led by Karisnik [as interpreted] or, further on, his deputy, Repija. That is why I said at the very beginning why I didn't want to take that unit in. Actually, when this unit was established, these 10 young men were supposed to be trained individually, with our assistance. Actually, each one of them was supposed to train other people. So then, ultimately, a unit was formed that existed of over 100 persons, on the basis of this attitude we had taken. We wished to turn this unit into a special-purposes unit. While I was in Sarajevo during that one month, we did not manage to do that. You had words of praise for the commanders, but my view is something different. I think that we stopped only halfway. This unit separated itself from the rest. They thought that they were well trained and that they had nothing else to learn. I think that they were not trained enough. The ten persons that the special unit at Krtelj had, and so many other good young men in different SUPs, those who knew how to shoot well, those who were well versed in the martial arts, out of all of these men a good special unit could have been formed that would have been the counterpart of the unit we had in Belgrade at the SUP, and, actually, all the special units in different units -- in different republics were based on that original unit from the Federal SUP.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is of utmost interest to me to have these proceedings take place in public. I respect witnesses, and all of those who respect me respect the witnesses, and I am proud of my friends and supporters, and I have to say that no witnesses so far have had any problems, and I believe that you will not have any problems either, although our views may differ. In a way, these are words of praise for my friends. It is only an enemy of mine that could cause any unpleasantness to any witness. Thank you, and I apologise for having squabbled with you over certain things. Perhaps it was a lack of precision and then I wanted things to be spelled out as clearly as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Davidovic. Mr. Davidovic, during --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, during cross-examination, Mr. Karadzic put to you a number of documents, mostly from 1994, related to the judiciary and the prosecution of perpetrators. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For the most part, it was 1994 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: During the first day of cross-examination, at transcript page 15678, Mr. Karadzic put to you a letter sent by the President's Office on 7th August 1994 to the VRS Main Staff Intelligence Department, asking them which steps had been taken in relation to the case of Nenad Milicic, commander of the VRS Brod Battalion. And Mr. Karadzic suggested to you that he had urged the judicial organs to speed up the procedure, and you agreed that the document showed an effort to establish legality. Could we now have 65 ter 22020 brought up on the screen. And as it is coming up: It is a document sent by the VRS Main Staff Intelligence Department to the President's Office on 5th June 1994 informing them of tasks in co-operation with the RS MUP State Security and Public Security departments in two specific cases. Mr. Davidovic, the first case listed under number 1 in this letter is a case of booby-trapping the car of Borivoje Djuric, president of the Deputies' Club of the SDS in Brod, and that the RDB organs learned about the involvement of the commander of the Brod Battalion of the Army of the Republika Srpska, Nenad Milicic, aka Neso, his assistant, and some other members in this sabotage act. Do you see this, Mr. Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, given the name and the position of that crime, would you be able to say whether this person was a Serb or a non-Serb?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if you now look at the second case mentioned in this document - it's under number 2 - it relates to a crime committed in Janja, and the victim is Reserve Police Officer Mirko Tomic, the owner of a catering business. Do you know Mr. Tomic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember who that is. It does ring a bell, the name, but at this moment I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What would be his ethnic origin, if you can tell by looking at his name?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can conclude that it is Mirko Tomic, an ethnic Serb. You can see that by his name. However, Mirko Tomic, before the war, did not have any kind of restaurant. I can claim with certainty that he either got it, or someone handed it over to him, or he usurped it. I cannot say. He became the owner of that restaurant, and that is not right. There were no Serb restaurants in Janja, and this is that period --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the rest of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can you -- the interpreters missed -- couldn't get all your answer. You said. "... this is that period --" And then they lost you. Could you complete that sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the period when that kind of thing could not happen in Janja. There was not a single catering establishment in Janja that was owned by the Serbs. This facility that is referred to as Marko Tomic's must have been received or usurped from a Muslim, and now this Mirko Tomic was running it. So it's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2924, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, Mr. Karadzic also put to you, and here it's transcript page 15681, a letter sent by him to the Supreme Military Court and the supreme military prosecutor of the RS on the 6th of September, 1994 - and that's Exhibit D01422 - asking them to explain why a trial involving 10 perpetrators, scheduled for the 26th of September, 1994, while the accused are free because the military prosecutor failed to file a motion for detention measures, and it also referred to the fact that seven of the perpetrators were kept in detention only briefly and three of them only for 30 days. Do you remember that you discussed this with Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. This is a document that confirms that he did this to see what the reasons are why some people are free and others are not, why they were released before the investigation was completed. And I think that that could be an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Can we please have 65 ter 23174 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up: It is another letter signed by Mr. Karadzic to the Supreme Military Court and the supreme military prosecutor of the RS, of the 31st of August, 1994, in which Mr. Karadzic stated that Radenko Renic had sent a letter to the President's office concerning the murder of his son Vojin Nenic [sic], whose killers were set free, still free, and were sending new threats to the family of the killed person. And if you look a little bit further down in the main paragraph in this letter, Mr. Karadzic states further that the VRS Main Staff Intelligence Sector had informed them that the murder had taken place on 5th July 1993 in the building of the Command of the 5th Battalion of the 2nd Brigade in Rijecani. And he refers also to the seven perpetrators were released the same day and three of them held 30 days. Mr. Davidovic, looking at the names of the victim and the father, what would be the ethnicity of Ranko Nenic [sic] and his son Vojin Nenic [sic]?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT REPORTER
utterances.text: Renic or Nenic?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Nenic. Oh, sorry, Renic. I misspoke. Renic. It says here Radenko Renic, at least in the version that I can read. The original I cannot read whether it says "Renic" or ... it says Renic. Renic, yes. Sorry. Renic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say for sure whether it's a Serb or a Croat. There are names that appear among both ethnic groups, so you cannot say for sure whether it's a Serb or a Croat name.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, you told us that you do not understand English. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No -- yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you kindly take off your headphones for a moment. Yes. Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, if you could tell us, in a brief manner, how this document and the previous document are relevant to your case.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The Prosecution's position is that the accused was able to influence and to direct authorities to investigate or prosecute. However, he chose to do that on a selective basis. And these documents are supposed to show that this was, in fact, the case; that when, here, for instance, the Serb is the victim, then there is intervention. And when it is not, then it's different. That is just two examples. As this is here a murder taking place in the Command of the 5th Battalion of the 2nd Brigade in Rijecani, there seems to be also the indication that this is, again, a Serb victim. The selective actions that he takes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can there be an answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. This is not a time for debate. We just wanted to know where she was going. You'll have another time to respond to the submission. Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: These are only two -- the two examples that I want to put in relation to this particular issue. And, Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2925, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The other topic that I would like to ask you about is the fact that -- who the person Vojkan Djurkovic was and whether he was promoted. At transcript pages 15712 to 15715, you discuss the promotion of Vojkan Djurkovic, and you made a reference to the video-clip depicting an award parade of Arkan's troop in Bijeljina, and you -- at page 15714, you said that he was standing there at the head. And also during the examination-in-chief, when we had a video, you mentioned his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have Exhibit P02858 be played, and only the first eight seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Davidovic, please say "stop" when you see the person by the name of Vojkan Djurkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to switch to Sanction first and start again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's the first one here, the first one on our right-hand side. As he is walking, he's the first one on the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And this -- what is the uniform and the flag that he is basically next to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the flag of Arkan's unit, the Panthers, and he is wearing a camouflage uniform with a beret. Officers wear red berets. Actually, they're a dark-cherry colour. And soldiers wear olive-grey berets. Actually, it can be seen even better in another situation, when they're coming from the mosque. That's where you can see Vojkan as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we move on and let it play a little bit further. And, please, again -- Your Honour, just for the record, so that you can identify this particular still, it is at 00:00:06.5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we just --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can clearly see Vojkan Djurkovic, very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes. What was it, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us avail ourselves of this opportunity. May we ask Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff to identify the date, the date when this happened, when this review took place, when this video-clip was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say. I cannot say the exact date. No chance of that. I can just confirm as I said earlier on, when I watched this video, you can see the monument in front of the municipality. That was placed there in 1993. When the unit is on the other side, when it's moving from the courthouse to the municipality building, then you can see the area where the mosque used to be, the one that was destroyed in 1993. And I see that the grass is green, so this review could be in 1994, but when exactly, I cannot say. You can see that it's green, it's not winter-time, so it's summer-time, spring, perhaps even autumn, because in the area where the mosque used to be, where everything was destroyed, grass was planted, and the grass grew out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution can say - thank you - it is their exhibit and they should have that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed, we do have this information, but I purposely didn't mention it because the witness didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The title says it was the 23rd of October, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's actually the 26th, so -- I can't see it now, but it should be the 26th of October, 1995, so a year later than the witness thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: At transcript page 15730, Mr. Karadzic told you that his office recorded every visit and every telephone call to him and that there was no trace of any contact between Vojkan Djurkovic and Mr. Karadzic. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember him saying it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 23081 be brought up in e-court. And, Your Honour, it is a document provided by Serbia on the 14th of March, 2007, and there are no protective measures related to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, looking at the first page: It is a document dated 9 April 1994, forwarded to Frenki, as it says on top left. This information mostly related to Western Slavonia. Mr. Davidovic, who -- do you know who is Frenki, where this document is forwarded to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Frenki Simatovic, assistant to Jovica Stanisic, an individual who was charged directly with planning, directing of all important matters, including logistics, for the Red Berets of the Security Service in the Republic of Serbia. So Frenki was the one who took care of everything, issued others, tours the area, and took care of everything that was of relevance to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have the last page in the B/C/S and page 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, the last paragraph in the document reads, and I quote here: "In Bijeljina, moving out of the Muslim families by the Exchange State Commission, led by Vojislav Djurkovic, aka Puskar or Vojka, still continues. However, the problem is that the said person takes 300 to 500 German marks per head for departure." And a line later there is a reference to the fact that he also takes money from Serbs moving into Muslim houses. Is this consistent with your own information?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke about it. When Vojkan would pick up Muslims and take them from their houses --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, we don't need to repeat this because you have already told these details. Just a bit further down, it says: "However, the entire time there is information that Puskar is acting under President Karadzic's orders and has to give him part of the money. Also, allegedly, he gives part of the money to Arkan, as he uses his people for the removes. That information wouldn't be significant if it was not for such a long time in Bijeljina and Janja, and for sure it was given also to the International Red Cross, as well as to the Muslims in Tuzla and Sarajevo and thus in Geneva. One delegate in the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia inquired about Puskar, his moving out of Muslims, and asked whose man he was, Milosevic's or Karadzic's." And the report is signed with the Greek letter sigma. Mr. Davidovic, do you know what the sigma sign at the end of the document stands for?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a code-sign that they used. Whenever you wrote "Sigma," it meant that the letter came from Frenki Simatovic and that he was the one signing it. So this code-name was assigned to an individual so you would know who would -- who signed it. I knew that it was Frenki Simatovic who was behind the sigma sign. Why they used it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But this information was supposed to be forwarded to Frenki. So, according to your explanation, something signed by himself is to be forwarded to Frenki. Could you expand on that, Mr. Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When a letter is sent from Frenki, there is always the sign there. Why, I don't know. I don't know who assigned the code to him, but I always was aware of the fact that the letter originated from him whenever "Sigma" was written on it. There was one of his men - I think his name was Carli - down in Sarajevo, and I asked him once because I saw a paper with the sign, and he said, It's from the commander. Why this letter has his name at the top, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Defence give their response to the request for admission of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Have you asked admission of this document, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, I did ask the admission of the document. And as I said before, it's a document provided by the Republic of Serbia according to an RFI of the Prosecutor's Office, and it was provided to us on the 14th of March, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. You're going to deal with --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I oppose the admission of the document. I can only anticipate that this is a group that we managed to destroy. I think Mr. Davidovic would know about this group. This document is not a credible one. From what I know, the group was, in fact, disbanded, dispersed, but we arrested the members of the group, and I believe that they continued feigning [as interpreted] to exist. I'm sure the gentleman here will know what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. If I could also add: I think this is a situation where a document would have so little weight that you should not admit it, as opposed to admitting it and then taking some of these issues under consideration as to weight, because, first of all, as you've already pointed out, its question as to the authorship, basically unknown. It's unlikely that Frenki would be writing to himself. Secondly, the information that the Prosecution wants to elicit from this document is also attributed to unknown individuals. It's basically gossip. So the probative value of this information is very, very low, and we ought to have the right to confront someone who actually has knowledge of this. There's no expectation that Mr. Davidovic would have ever seen this document or had anything to do with it. It's just simply he's being used as a convenient vehicle to refute something that was suggested to him through a document that there's no expectation that he has any knowledge of, and it denies us our right to confront the person with that kind of information. So when you add all those factors together, I think that the probative value of this document is out-weighed by its prejudicial effect and that it ought not to be admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I also answer this. And I would suggest that you, perhaps, not make, right now, a decision, but, rather, wait until I show the next document to the witness, because it is related and clarifies the group Sigma and who the group Sigma is. And I also want to mention that the witness has basically said what is written here is exactly what he also says and noticed. I think that's how it relates to the witness, as such. But in as to the value of this document, I would suggest that you perhaps let me show the next document and then you make your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, let's proceed, then, with the next one, the next document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Can we please have 65 ter 2315 -- 23015 on the screen. And it is again from the Republic of Serbia, and it has a few redactions in there; basically, the people signing it and the -- yeah, that's on the last page, a few redactions. And as it is coming up: It is a document from the State Security Department -- from the State Security Department of the Republic of Serbia, dated the 27th June, 1994. It discusses the problems of the intelligence group with the pseudonym "Typhoon," and it says that they had approached the 2nd Administration of the RDB of the Republic of Serbia MUP for co-operation. Can we have the three last paragraphs focused on. And in the B/C/S it's actually spreading into the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It says here that: "We let the members of the group known that we will accept the group's initiative only under the conditions that they get approval from the president of the Republika Srpska, Radovan Karadzic, and the minister of interior, Mr. Stanisic." And then it states further that this group has Karadzic and Stanisic's approval that they will be incorporated into the system under Franko Simatovic. They will have the pseudonym "Sigma." Mr. Davidovic --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask that the dates of these documents be indicated? If Madam Uertz-Retzlaff thinks that one document arises from the other, can we have the dates for both of the documents and so we can see for ourselves?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I've actually mentioned the date. Here, it's the 27th June 1994, and the previous one was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- the 9th of April, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Davidovic, do you know about a group, Typhoon, and, as it says here, renamed then to "Sigma"? Do you know anything about such intelligence groups providing information to Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and I can't claim this with any certainty, the Typhoon group was a group of individuals who were unhappy with certain developments in Banja Luka, both in the military and civilian authorities, and as a result they launched a revolt initiative asking for the president of the municipality and some other individuals to step down. They called themselves the Typhoon Group. Apparently, they wanted some wrongs to be righted, and they pointed their fingers at individuals in the army and civilian authorities for fraud and unlawful activities. After a while, a compromise was reached. Was somebody arrested, was somebody brought in? At any rate, things settled down. I know that the group was active in Banja Luka and operated for a while and suited up with the Army of Republika Srpska as well as Mr. Karadzic and his followers from the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have this document as well admitted, and I think it has now shed more clarity on Sigma.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This document, we don't have any objection to this being admitted, but I think that it shows that the other document is even more unreliable than we thought, because now it's being authored by some group that's in opposition -- in political opposition to President Karadzic. And I think it's a serious allegation that's contained in the other document, that President Karadzic somehow was complicit in the extorting of money from Muslims, and in order for anything like that to even be remotely considered by this Trial Chamber, we ought to have the chance to confront it. And this witness knows nothing about the source of that information, and the document itself is extremely -- has such low weight that it ought not to be admitted in this trial without someone here that we can confront so that you could have some analysis of what weight to give to that information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just can I ask one question to Mr. Davidovic. Pursuant to this document we are seeing now, the penultimate sentence in English: "The technical aspects of two-way communication were accordingly studied, and the group will from now on contact us under the pseudonym 'Sigma'." So "Sigma" was allegedly introduced/established in sometime June, but do you know that "Sigma" was used before this time-period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I remember seeing documents with that code, and I didn't know what it stood for. I was told that this had to do with documents that were related to the commander, Simatovic. I don't know the details of it. But I did have occasion to see a document - I held it in my hands - belonging to a member of the Red Berets which had this sign on it, and I didn't know what it stood for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As to the first document, the Chamber hasn't reached a consensus. We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P2927, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the second document will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2926.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I then have a couple of minutes for a re-cross only on this particular issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On the issue of this alleged Sigma? I will consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic, do you know that I ordered for the Typhoon group to be re-subordinated to the Ministry of the Interior and the State Security Service and, when this was not done, ordered that they be disbanded, and when this wasn't done either, Deputy Minister Kovac reported to me that they continued operating and I asked and ordered that they be arrested, which ultimately they were? Did you have this information?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must admit that I know the matter only superficially. I know that there were problems. I know that measures were taken to stop them, to restrain them. Was an order issued for them to be disbanded? I don't know. I don't know about the arrests. I know that problems arose, but I wasn't able to follow the specific issue. I wasn't there. I only know what I was able to tell you now, in general terms. I was aware of the problems, though. I even said, in respect of one of your earlier documents, that there was this revolt on the part of some individuals who asked for people who were involved in crime to be removed. Subsequent problems emerged, barricades, et cetera. I am not aware of these steps that were taken. It is possible that they were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another question. Had you received this letter, would you have believed them on what they said, that I allowed them to be integrated into the system?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that the consent has to be received from you or the minister.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch whether the witness said he would have believed them or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say, Thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said, Thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. The interpreter didn't hear what the witness said as to whether you would have believed them or not. And if I recall what the witness said, well, the matter has to be checked. And had the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I will deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your answer to the last question is noted as follows: "Well, I know that the consent has to be received from you or the minister." Did you say anything in addition to that, Mr. Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DAVIDOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that in principle, it has to be checked. It's not enough for someone to say that they've received consent from someone. You have to check it, you have to double-check it, in order to know whether a letter of this sort by a group is credible or not. I don't know if the other side believed them or not. I can only see what this one side said; that they had received consent. So what should have been done, as a rule, was to send a letter to the authority who apparently issued the consent. So you have to have a confirmation. You can't just trust a letter coming from Pero Peric unless you actually double-check whether it is credible or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That really concludes your evidence, Mr. Davidovic. On behalf of this Bench and the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for your coming all the way to The Hague to give it, and now you are free to go. Please have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, now Mr. Gaynor and I have to switch the positions, and also the next witness has protective measures. So some things have to be done; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably -- I'm minded to give a ruling in relation to the next witness. And then before we bring him in, I think we'll have a break so that everything can be adjusted. I'm wondering whether this should be in private session or not. But there's another matter we need to deal with in private session, so let's go into private session first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session. On 30th June 2011, the accused filed a motion for reconsideration of protective measures for Witness KDZ531, contesting the fact that the Chamber had granted Witness KDZ531 the protective measures of delayed disclosure of identity until 30 days before testimony and requesting that the Chamber hold a hearing in the presence of the witness to determine whether he can testify with less stringent protective measures. The accused submits that the Chamber should examine this motion de novo, and not under the "reconsideration" test, as the basis on which the contested decision was made was ex parte the accused. Also, on 30th of June, the Prosecution filed its response, arguing that the motion should be denied, as the accused has failed to meet the test for reconsideration, in that the Pre-Trial Chamber properly considered the information in relation to KDZ531's request for protective measures and correctly applied the relevant protective measure rules. First, the Chamber considers that the accused's motion is, indeed, a motion for reconsideration of its decision of 5th of June, 2009, regardless of the fact that the Prosecution's filing upon which the Chamber decision was made was kept ex parte. The Chamber notes that in its response for protective measures for Witness KDZ531, the accused did not provide his position on the trial-related protective measures, but only opposed the delayed disclosure request. The Chamber recalls that in its decision of 5th of June, 2009, it found that the pseudonym and closed session were appropriate measures and were necessary to safe-guard the privacy and protection of KDZ531 and his family. It also found that such measures were consistent with the rights of the accused in the present case. In coming to this conclusion, the Chamber carefully examined all the information presented to it and weighed against the rights of the accused. The Chamber, therefore, denies the accused's motion to reconsider the protective measures for KDZ531, on the grounds that the accused has not demonstrated that there was a clear error of reasoning in the Chamber's decision of 5th of June, 2009, and that given the current concerns expressed by the witness, the Chamber is not satisfied that it is necessary to reconsider its decision, to prevent injustice. That's the ruling. We'll have a break for --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just ask that the portion of today's proceedings that we just went into private session be provided to Professor Seselj. I think that since we discussed his case, and I think that also he'd be interested to know that what had occurred in connection with the Prosecution's dealing with the protected witness in his case, given the contempt proceedings against him, so I think it's only fair that the private session that we just had be made available to Professor Seselj so that he could have that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I was simply going to say that until the protective measures have been rescinded, I believe that the transcript should remain confidential, just should the Trial Chamber in the Seselj case decide not to rescind the protective measures. Now, after the protective measures are rescinded, if that's what the Seselj Trial Chamber decides to do, we have no objection to the portion being made public.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking it to be made public, Mr. President. I'm asking it to be disclosed at this stage to Professor Seselj so that he can have knowledge of that for whatever steps he may wish to take in connection with his own cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, if I may respond to that. That would still be a violation of the protective measures in place in the Seselj case. The Seselj Trial Chamber would probably object to that move, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider the matter. Yes, we'll have a break. Shall we break until 11.00? Yes, a bit more than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 4th day of July, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.05 p.m.,
